verification.result: All magnetic Seitz tables close modulo integer primitive translations. Every ordinary SG operation agrees with the corresponding type-I MSG rotation and translation.

apiCoverage.browser: Extracted symbol and BNS/OG lookup datasets.
Stored Seitz operations, numerical reciprocal-space action and little-group filtering.
Independent numerical finite-group/projective representation calculation; outputs D/C numerical labels, not BC/CDML/Bilbao labels.
Numerical induction and star-product tools have their own browser API; they are not Wolfram function calls.
Both original numeric text formats parsed by trace-parser.js; max 10 MiB. BC rotation/translation and spin-frame compatibility checked before matching.

Imported unitary characters can be decomposed against computed ordinary irreps or magnetic corepresentation restrictions, with Wigner-type normalization. No loading of libMLGCorep.mx, no guarantee of original corep labels.
Not ported: no automatic POSCAR/cell/origin/spin-frame standardization or Wolfram binary database import.

conventions: BC primitive-cell fractional real-space and reciprocal-space coordinates. Magnetic data use the BNS family primitive basis.
Translation phases exp(-2 pi i k dot t). Stored translations recovered exactly from upstream decimals with denominator dividing 12.
Stored spatial spin matrices use down-up basis and upstream six-decimal precision. Antiunitary flag is separate; time-reversal spin action is not pre-multiplied.
Trace input spin matrices use up-down basis. Matching swaps basis, detects the double-cover sign and corrects integer-lattice translation phases.
Lattice basis values in browser display are representative parameters, not a measured crystal structure.
limitations: Browser calculations are numerical and have bounded runtime; symbolic parameter families are not reproduced.
Numerical irreducible representation labels and gauges need not match the original Mathematica labels and bases.
A trace file in another cell/origin or Cartesian spin frame is rejected rather than silently transformed.
Magnetic band decomposition uses unitary restrictions of computed corepresentations with Wigner-type normalization; an incomplete Kramers/antiunitary multiplet is rejected.
